title: Mathematics 1
target_note: About 90 seconds a question. Nothing beyond GCSE technique; every mark is in the reading and the setup.

questions.stem_html:
A solid cube of side 2 cm has mass 40 g. A larger solid cube of the same material has mass 5 kg.

What is the side length of the larger cube?
questions.solution_html:
Density = 40/8 = 5 g/cm3. Volume of larger cube = 5000/5 = 1000 cm3, so side = 10 cm.

Or: mass ratio 125 = 53, so lengths scale by 5.

traps.B: 5 is the length scale factor, not the side length.
traps.C: Used volume ratio 1000 for the length scale.
traps.E: Confused grams and kilograms by a factor of 10.

questions.stem_html: Work out (3 × 108)26 × 105, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.solution_html: 9 × 1016 ÷ 6 × 105 = 1.5 × 1011. 1.5 × 1011

traps.E: Equal in value but not in standard form (needs 1 ≤ a < 10).

questions.stem_html: Express 0.2777… (with the 7 recurring) as a fraction in its lowest terms.
questions.solution_html: Let x = 0.2777…; 10x = 2.777…, 100x = 27.777…, so 90x = 25 and x = 25/90 = 5/18.

traps.E: Arithmetic slip in 25/90.

questions.stem_html:
Two positive integers a and b with a < b have highest common factor 6 and lowest common multiple 180.

How many such pairs (a, b) are there?
questions.solution_html:
Write a = 6p, b = 6q with p, q coprime. Then LCM = 6pq = 180, so pq = 30 = 2 × 3 × 5.

Coprime splits of 30 with p < q: (1, 30), (2, 15), (3, 10), (5, 6). 4 pairs.

traps.B: Missed the splits that move a single prime.
traps.E: 8 counts ordered pairs (a, b) and (b, a) separately.

questions.stem_html:
x = 4.5 and y = 2.0, both correct to 1 decimal place.

What is the upper bound of xy?
questions.solution_html: Largest x over smallest y: 4.55/1.95 = 455/195 = 91/39 = 7/3.

traps.B: 4.55/2.05, the upper bound of x over the upper bound of y.
traps.E: 4.45/2.05, lower over upper: the lower bound of the quotient.

questions.stem_html:
A price is reduced by 20% and then increased by p%. The final price is 10% more than the original.

What is p?
questions.solution_html: 0.8(1 + p/100) = 1.1, so 1 + p/100 = 1.375. p = 37.5.

traps.E: Assumed the 20% cut needs a 25% rise to undo, then added 10 + 5.

questions.stem_html: y is inversely proportional to x2. When x increases by 25%, by what percentage does y decrease?
questions.solution_html: x → 1.25x, so y → y/1.252 = y/1.5625 = 0.64y. Decrease of 36%.

traps.A: 25% is the change in x, not in y.
traps.D: 1.25² − 1 = 0.5625, the increase in x², not the decrease in y.
traps.E: 0.64 is the multiplier, not the decrease.

questions.stem_html: A quantity decreases by 10% every hour. After how many whole hours is it first less than half its starting value?

traps.E: Linear thinking with 5% steps.

questions.stem_html:
Simplify fully

x2 − 9x2 − x − 6 ÷ x + 3x2 − 4
questions.solution_html: (x − 3)(x + 3)(x − 3)(x + 2) × (x − 2)(x + 2)x + 3 = x − 2.

traps.C: Cancelled the wrong factor of x² − 4.
traps.D: Forgot to invert the second fraction properly.
traps.E: Left the x + 3 in the numerator.

questions.stem_html: Make a the subject of v = √a + ba − b.
questions.solution_html: v2(a − b) = a + b, so a(v2 − 1) = b(v2 + 1). a = b(v² + 1)/(v² − 1)

traps.D: Did not factor b out correctly.
traps.E: Dropped the a on the right.

questions.stem_html:
The line y = 2x − 1 meets the circle x2 + y2 = 13 at two points.

What is the sum of the x-coordinates of these points?
questions.solution_html: x2 + 4x2 − 4x + 1 = 13, so 5x2 − 4x − 12 = 0, (5x + 6)(x − 2) = 0. Sum = 2 − 6/5 = 4/5.

traps.E: Used the y-coordinates' difference or a factorisation slip.

questions.stem_html:
The curve y = 2x2 − 8x + 5 is reflected in the x-axis.

What is the maximum value of y on the reflected curve?
questions.solution_html: 2x2 − 8x + 5 = 2(x − 2)2 − 3, minimum −3. Reflection gives maximum 3.

traps.E: The y-intercept.

questions.stem_html: The first five terms of a quadratic sequence are 2, 7, 16, 29, 46. What is the 20th term?
questions.solution_html: Second differences are 4, so the n2 coefficient is 2. Subtracting 2n2 leaves 0, −1, −2, −3, −4 = 1 − n. Term = 2n2 − n + 1. n = 20: 800 − 20 + 1 = 781.

questions.stem_html: How many pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 2x + 3y ≤ 12 ?
questions.solution_html: y = 1: 2x ≤ 9, x = 1, 2, 3, 4. y = 2: 2x ≤ 6, three values. y = 3: 2x ≤ 3, one value. y = 4: none. Total 8.

traps.E: Included both axis points.

questions.stem_html: The line through (2, 3) perpendicular to 3x − 2y = 7 crosses the x-axis at (k, 0). What is k?
questions.solution_html: Given line has gradient 3/2, so the perpendicular has gradient −2/3: y − 3 = −(2/3)(x − 2). y = 0 gives x − 2 = 9/2, x = 13/2.

traps.A: The x-coordinate of the given point.

questions.stem_html: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 4 times each exterior angle. What is the sum of the interior angles of the polygon?
questions.solution_html: Interior + exterior = 180°, so exterior = 36°, giving 360/36 = 10 sides. Sum = 180 × 8 = 1440°.

traps.E: 12 sides (exterior 30°).

questions.stem_html:
In the diagram, the line through A is a tangent to the circle at A. B and C lie on the circle with AB = AC, and the angle between the tangent and AB is 65°.

What is angle BAC?

<circle cx="160" cy="120" r="70" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.6"/>

questions.stem_html: Two similar cones have surface areas in the ratio 4 : 9. The smaller cone has volume 16 cm3. What is the volume of the larger cone?
questions.solution_html: Length ratio 2 : 3, volume ratio 8 : 27. 16 × 27/8 = 54.

traps.A: Used the length ratio 2 : 3 for volumes.
traps.E: 81 = 16 × 81/16, using 9² as the volume factor.

questions.detail: Similar solids: area and volume scale factors

questions.stem_html:
The diagram shows a cube of side 2. A is a vertex and M is the midpoint of the vertical edge furthest from A.

What is the length AM?
questions.diagram_svg:

<g fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.6"><polygon points="60,190 180,190 180,70 60,70"/><polygon points="180,190 240,150 240,30 180,70"/><polygon points="60,70 180,70 240,30 120,30"/></g>

<g fill="#111"><circle cx="60" cy="190" r="2.8"/><circle cx="240" cy="90" r="2.8"/></g>
<g font-family="Georgia,serif" font-style="italic" font-size="15" fill="#111"><text x="44" y="206">A</text><text x="248" y="95">M</text></g>
<g font-family="Arial" font-size="13" fill="#111"><text x="112" y="208">2</text><text x="264" y="70">2</text></g></svg>
questions.solution_html: Put A at (0, 0, 0). The far vertical edge runs from (2, 2, 0) to (2, 2, 2), so M = (2, 2, 1). AM = √4 + 4 + 1 = 3.

traps.D: Used the far vertex's height 2 with one dimension dropped.
traps.E: The space diagonal to the far vertex, not its midpoint edge.

questions.stem_html:
In triangle ABC, angle B = 45° and angle C = 60°. The perpendicular from A to BC has length 6.

What is the length of BC?
questions.solution_html: Let the foot be D. In the 45° triangle, BD = 6. In the 60° triangle, DC = 6/tan 60° = 6/√3 = 2√3. BC = 6 + 2√3.

traps.C: Used 6 × tan 30° = 2√3 correctly but then added 3√3 by a slip.
traps.E: Used the slant sides AB and AC instead of the base.

questions.detail: Exact trig values in a composite triangle

questions.stem_html: A sector of a circle of radius 12 cm with angle 120° is folded to make a cone (the two straight edges are joined). What is the vertical height of the cone?
questions.solution_html: Arc length = (120/360) × 2π × 12 = 8π = circumference of the base, so base radius = 4. Slant height = 12. Height = √144 − 16 = √128 = 8√2 cm.

traps.C: √80 from an arc-length slip giving radius 8.

questions.stem_html:
OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB and P lies on OM with OP : PM = 2 : 1.

Express AP in terms of a and b.
questions.solution_html: OM = ½(a + b), OP = ⅔OM = ⅓(a + b). AP = OP − a = ⅓(b − 2a).

traps.D: AM direction with the wrong scale.
traps.E: PA, the reverse vector.

questions.stem_html: The mean of 10 numbers is 6. The mean of the 4 smallest is 2 and the mean of the 4 largest is 11. What is the mean of the other 2 numbers?
questions.solution_html: Total 60. Smallest four sum to 8, largest four to 44. Remaining two sum to 8, mean 4.

traps.D: Assumed the middle pair has the overall mean.
traps.E: The sum of the remaining two, not the mean.

questions.stem_html: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue counters. Three are taken at random without replacement. What is the probability that exactly two are red?
questions.solution_html: P(RRB in a given order) = (5/8)(4/7)(3/6) = 60/336 = 5/28. Three orders: 15/28.

questions.stem_html: In a class of 30, 18 study French, 15 study Spanish and 5 study neither. A student who studies French is chosen at random. What is the probability that they also study Spanish?

traps.E: 8/15, conditioned on Spanish instead.

questions.detail: Conditional probability from a two-way table

questions.stem_html: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. What is the probability that the product of the two scores is a multiple of 6?
questions.solution_html: Pairs containing a 6: 6 + 6 − 1 = 11. Pairs with no 6 whose product is a multiple of 6 need a 3 and an even number from {2, 4}: (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 3), (3, 4): 4 more. 15/36 = 5/12.

questions.stem_html: N is the smallest positive integer such that 2N is a square number and 3N is a cube number. What is N?
questions.solution_html:
Let N = 2a3b. 2N square: a + 1 even, b even. 3N cube: a a multiple of 3, b + 1 a multiple of 3.

Smallest: a = 3, b = 2. N = 8 × 9 = 72. Check: 144 = 122, 216 = 63.

traps.A: 2 × 18 = 36 is square but 3 × 18 = 54 is not a cube.
traps.E: 2 × 144 = 288 is not a square.
